text:
ella.sr-sales: Hey team, prospect (FinPay) ran a short POC and saw big tail latency variance at ~95th-99th percentiles. Asking us for a short writeup: why, how we'd fix it, and what it means for pricing/commit. Can we sync quick?
marc.sre: Thanks — can you paste the load plan they ran? qps, seq len, model, concurrent clients?
ella.sr-sales: Copy from them: 
  - model: open-redwood-7b-v1 (non-quant)
  - qps: burst to 120, steady 60
  - concurrency: 24 clients
  - input tokens: mean 120, max 480
  - batching: client-side only (no server batching)
  - test length: 30m
marc.sre: OK that explains a lot. long tails usually from uneven batching + KV cache misses at larger seqs. Also warmup was short so Xen VM scheduling + GPU memory pressure likely contributed.
priya.se: Agreed. Quick remediation plan for them: 
  1) enable server-side continuous batching (reduce tail by ~30-50% typical)
  2) enable prefix/KV caching for repeated convo patterns (if applicable)
  3) pin a quantized variant (int8) for throughput-sensitive endpoints
  4) increase warmup to 10 min with ramped traffic
 5) if strict 99.9 SLO, consider Dedicated pool with pinned GPUs
jordan.ml: Adding model notes: open-redwood-7b-v1 int8 loses ~0.5-1% quality on our evals but gives ~2.5x tokens/sec improvement on A100ish. For tail reduction, batching+cache is bigger win than quant alone.
ankit.sales-eng: Pricing re: Dedicated vs Hosted: rough back-of-envelope — to hit consistent sub-200ms p50 and good p95 at their qps, Dedicated with a 3-card GPU pool recommended. ~ $Xk/mo committed — I can run exact numbers if we get target SLO and 30-day qps curve. Hosted will be cheaper initially but can hit tail spikes and throttling during bursts.
lisa.ciso: Security checklist they asked: do we persist prompt data? are logs stored in their region? SAML/SCIM for SSO? Audit logs retention? They need answers for procurement.
ella.sr-sales: They specifically asked whether Dedicated helps with data residency and auditability. Also want to know if enabling KV cache stores any PII server-side.
priya.se: Dedicated gives stronger isolation and easier VPC routing — routing logs remain customer-owned when Private/Dedicated + VPC peering. KV cache stores encoded KV for model attention (not human-readable) but we can disable cache if they want zero server-side state. Document that for security.
marc.sre: Test plan I'd propose for their next run (30-60m): 
  - ramp 0->60 qps over 5m, hold 20m, burst to 120 qps for 2x1m bursts every 5m
  - use server-side batching (batch timeout 10ms) and enable KV cache for repeated sessions
  - collect p50/p90/p95/p99/p999, gpu util, batch sizes, latency distribution by seq len
  - warmup with identical traffic for 10m before measurement window
  - attach tracer id in headers so we can correlate traces in console
priya.se: Example curl snippet for their devs to hit the batching endpoint:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"open-redwood-7b-v1-int8","prompt":"<prompt>","max_tokens":256,"client_id":"finpay-test"}'
ankit.sales-eng: Also note cost impact of KV cache: it reduces token unit cost effectively by lowering compute per token. The billing delta between hosted non-quant and int8 dedicated is typically: hosted non-quant ~ baseline X, int8 hosted ~ 0.4X, dedicated int8 ~ 0.25X per-token (depends on commit). I'll follow up with numbers.
lisa.ciso: For procurement: send a short one-pager stating: data residency options, SSO + SCIM support, retention defaults + custom retention, how to request HSM/KMS keys. I can draft if you want.
ella.sr-sales: Yes please — a one-pager would be perfect. Also need a short plain-English summary of the latency fixes and tradeoffs to share with their infra lead.
priya.se: Draft summary (shareable):
  - Observed cause: tail variance caused by short warmup, client-side only batching, and mixed sequence lengths that produce uneven GPU kernel timings.
  - Quick fixes (low lift): enable server-side continuous batching (10ms), increase warmup to 10min, add KV caching for hot prefixes. Expected p95 improvement 30-60%.
  - Medium lift: switch to int8 quantized model -> higher throughput, small quality delta (~0.5-1%). Expected combined p95 improvement 50-80%.
  - When to pick Dedicated: if you need strict SLOs for p99/p999 or data residency/isolated tenancy — Dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor variability and gives more predictable tails.
  - Cost note: switching to int8 lowers per-token compute; Dedicated is more cost-predictable with commit discounts but higher fixed cost.
marc.sre: I'll prepare a short Grafana dashboard snapshot template for them (latency percentiles + batch size heatmap + GPU util).
ankit.sales-eng: I'll calculate a sample three-month committed quote vs hosted run-rate and share in thread tomorrow.
lisa.ciso: I'll draft the security one-pager and drop in here by EOD.
ella.sr-sales: Perfect — this gives me everything to reply to FinPay. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
loadtest-bot: loadtest completed: run_id=rt-20240203-19, failures=0, avg_latency=132ms, p95=420ms, p99=980ms
ella.sr-sales: Adding the bot summary for their logs. Going to send the one-pager + short plan to FinPay and request a rerun with the updated config.
priya.se: If they want, we can run a managed POC with our SEs applying the changes and provide results in 24-48h.
ella.sr-sales: Let's offer managed run as an add-on. Thanks team.
